\chapter{Complexity — Counter Prog Run}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CounterProgRun
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module provides Hoare-style reasoning about runs of unary counter programs
(goto programs over natural-number registers that read a binary input once and
print bits or register values in unary), the programming model for the
polynomial-time emitters of Arora--Barak, \S6.2, Remark~6.7.  It introduces the
run relation ``from this label and these registers the program reaches that label
and those registers, printing $e$, within $b$ steps'', its composition, one rule
per instruction, the count-down loop, straight-line templates of print
micro-operations, and linear expressions in the registers printed in unary; it
also shows that a halting run of $t$ abstract steps is a computation of the
compiled multi-tape Turing machine within $t(2t+3)$ steps, and bounds the growth
of the input position and of the output along a run.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Run relation of a counter program]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.run}
Let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ natural-number registers with label set
$\Lambda$, run on a binary input $x$.  Given a label $\ell \in \Lambda$, a target
$\ell' \in \Lambda \cup \{\bot\}$ (where $\bot$ means halted), register vectors
$\rho, \rho' : \{0,\dots,R-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$, input positions $p, p' \in
\mathbb{N}$, a bit string $e$ and a bound $b \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the
predicate that for every output $o$ printed so far there is some $t \le b$ such
that $t$ steps of $P$ on $x$ lead from the state with label $\ell$, registers
$\rho$, $p$ input symbols read and output $o$ to the state with label $\ell'$,
registers $\rho'$, $p'$ input symbols read and output $o\,e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Composition of counter-program runs]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.trans}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.trans}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.run_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ natural-number registers and labels in $\Lambda$,
run on a binary input $x$. Suppose that every output word $o$ admits a run of at most
$b$ steps from $\ell,\rho,p,o$ to $\ell',\rho',p'$ with output $o$ followed by $e$,
and that every output word admits a run of at most $b'$ steps from $\ell',\rho',p'$ to
$\ell''$ (a label or halt), $\rho''$, and $p''$, appending $e'$. Then every $o$ admits a
run of at most $b+b'$ steps from $\ell,\rho,p,o$ to $\ell'',\rho'',p''$, with output $o$
followed by the concatenation $e$ and $e'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the run bound]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.mono}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes}
\difficulty{2}
Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ natural-number registers and labels in $\Lambda$,
run on a binary input $x$. If for every output word $o$ some run of at most $b$ steps
from label $\ell$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$ reaches $\ell'$,
$\rho'$, and $p'$ while appending $e$, and $b\le b'$, then the same endpoints and output
extension are reachable within $b'$ steps for every $o$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Changing run endpoints]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.congr}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.mono}
\difficulty{2}
Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ natural-number registers and labels in $\Lambda$,
run on a binary input $x$. Suppose that for every output word $o$, some run of at most
$b$ steps from label $\ell$, register assignment $\rho$, input position $p$, and output
$o$ reaches label-or-halt state $\ell'$, assignment $\rho'$, position $p'$, and output
$o$ followed by $e$. If $\rho=\sigma$, $\rho'=\sigma'$, $p=q$, $p'=q'$, $e=e'$, and
$b\le b'$, then for every $o$ some run of at most $b'$ steps from $\ell,\sigma,q,o$
reaches $\ell',\sigma',q'$ with output $o$ followed by $e'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A one-step transition gives a bounded run]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with initial label $\ell$, register
assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$, and target label-or-halted-state $q$,
register assignment $\rho'$, input position $p'$, and output string $e$. Suppose that
for every output string $o$, one step from the state with label $\ell$, registers
$\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ yields the state with label-or-halted-state
$q$, registers $\rho'$, input position $p'$, and output $o$ followed by $e$. Then from
that initial state the program reaches the specified target state within at most one
step, appending $e$ to every initial output string.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run rule for a halt instruction]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_halt}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, and let $\rho$ be a register
assignment, $p$ an input position, and $\ell\in\Lambda$ a label. If the instruction at
$\ell$ is to halt, then for every output string $o$, the program reaches the halted
state with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ within at most one step.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run rule for a goto instruction]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_goto}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_goto}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, and let $\rho$ be a register
assignment, $p$ an input position, and $\ell,\ell'\in\Lambda$ labels. If the
instruction at $\ell$ is to jump to $\ell'$, then for every output string $o$, the
program reaches label $\ell'$ with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$
within at most one step.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run rule for printing a bit]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_out}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_out}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with label $\ell$, destination label
$\ell'$, bit $b$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$. If the instruction
at $\ell$ prints $b$ and then goes to $\ell'$, then for every output string $o$, within
at most one step the program reaches $\ell'$ with registers $\rho$, input position $p$,
and output $o$ followed by $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run rule for incrementing a register]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_inc}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_inc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with label $\ell$, destination label
$\ell'$, register $r$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$. If the
instruction at $\ell$ increments register $r$ and then goes to $\ell'$, then for every
output string $o$, within at most one step the program reaches $\ell'$ with input
position $p$, output $o$, and registers equal to $\rho$ except that register $r$ has
value $\rho(r)+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step decrement behavior]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_dec}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_dec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on input $x$, let $\ell,\ell'$ be labels, let $\rho$ be
register values, and let $p$ be the input read position. If the instruction at $\ell$ is
to decrement register $r$ and continue at $\ell'$, then for every current output string
$o$ there is a run of at most one step from label $\ell$, registers $\rho$, read
position $p$, and output $o$ to label $\ell'$, with register $r$ decreased by one with
zero truncated at zero, all other registers unchanged, the same read position, and
output still $o$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_jz_zero}

Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with label $\ell$, register $r$,
labels $\ell_0,\ell_1$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$. Suppose the
instruction at $\ell$ branches to $\ell_0$ when register $r$ is zero and to $\ell_1$

step the program reaches $\ell_0$ with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero test on a nonzero register]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_jz_pos}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_jz_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with label $\ell$, register $r$,
labels $\ell_0,\ell_1$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$. Suppose the

\begin{theorem}[Unary register printing in one step]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_pr}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_pr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with registers $\rho$ and labels
$\Lambda$. If the instruction at label $\ell$ prints register $r$ in unary and then goes
to $\ell'$, then from any output string $o$, the program reaches label $\ell'$ within
one step, with registers and input position unchanged and with $1^{\rho(r)}$ appended to
the output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reading at the end of the input]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_rd_end}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_rd_end}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with registers $\rho$ and labels
$\Lambda$. If the instruction at label $\ell$ reads the next input bit and the input has

$\ell_e$ within one step, leaving the registers, input position, and output unchanged.

\begin{theorem}[Reading a zero from the input]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_rd_false}

\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with registers $\rho$ and labels
$\Lambda$. If the instruction at label $\ell$ reads the next input bit and the bit at

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reading a one from the input]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_rd_true}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_rd_true}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_of_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with registers $\rho$ and labels
$\Lambda$. If the instruction at label $\ell$ reads the next input bit and the bit at

\begin{theorem}[A counter program count-down loop]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_loop}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_loop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.congr, Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.trans, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_dec, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_jz_pos, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_jz_zero}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with labels $h,d,c,z$ and register
$r$. Suppose the instruction at $h$ tests $r$, going to $z$ if it is zero and to $d$
otherwise, and the instruction at $d$ decrements $r$ and goes to $c$. Let
$K,b\in\mathbb{N}$, and for each $j\in\mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma_j$ be a register
assignment, $p_j$ an input position, and $e_j$ an output string. Assume
$\sigma_j(r)=K-j$ for every $j\le K$, and that for every $j<K$, from label $c$ with
register assignment obtained from $\sigma_j$ by setting register $r$ to $K-j-1$ and
input position $p_j$, the program reaches label $h$ with registers $\sigma_{j+1}$ and
input position $p_{j+1}$ within at most $b$ steps, appending $e_j$ to every initial
output string. Then from label $h$ with registers $\sigma_0$ and input position $p_0$,
the program reaches label $z$ with registers $\sigma_K$ and input position $p_K$ within
at most $K(b+2)+1$ steps, appending the concatenation of $e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_{K-1}$ to
every initial output string.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Template micro-operation]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp}
\leanok
For $R \in \mathbb{N}$, a template micro-operation over $R$ registers is either
$\mathsf{out}(b)$ for a bit $b$, meaning ``print the bit $b$'', or
$\mathsf{pr}(r)$ for a register index $r < R$, meaning ``print the value of
register $r$ in unary''.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output of a micro-operation]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp.exec}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp.exec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp}
Given register values $\rho : \{0,\dots,R-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$, the string printed
by a template micro-operation is defined by: $\mathsf{out}(b)$ prints the
one-symbol string $b$, and $\mathsf{pr}(r)$ prints $1^{\rho(r)}$, the string of
$\rho(r)$ ones.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Instruction of a template at a position]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.tmplInstr}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.tmplInstr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Instr, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp}
Given a list $\tau = (m_0, \dots, m_{n-1})$ of template micro-operations, labels
$\lambda : \mathbb{N} \to \Lambda$ and a continuation label $\nu$, the
counter-program instruction at index $i$ is: $\mathsf{out}(b, \lambda(i+1))$
(print $b$, go to $\lambda(i+1)$) if $i < n$ and $m_i = \mathsf{out}(b)$;
$\mathsf{pr}(r, \lambda(i+1))$ (print register $r$ in unary, go to
$\lambda(i+1)$) if $i < n$ and $m_i = \mathsf{pr}(r)$; and $\mathsf{goto}\ \nu$
if $i \ge n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Execution of a template sequence]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_tmpl}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.goes_tmpl}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.mono, Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.trans, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp.exec, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_goto, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_out, Complexity.CounterProg.goes_pr, Complexity.CounterProg.tmplInstr}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, and let $\tau$ be a list of $n$
micro-operations, each printing a bit or printing a register in unary. Let
$lab:\mathbb{N}\to\Lambda$ be labels and let $\nu\in\Lambda$. Suppose that at every
index $i\le n$, the instruction at $lab(i)$ is the instruction prescribed by the
template at $i$: it performs the corresponding micro-operation and goes to $lab(i+1)$
when $i<n$, and goes to $\nu$ when $i=n$. Then, for every register assignment $\rho$ and
input position $p$, from label $lab(0)$ the program reaches $\nu$ within $n+1$ steps,
with the register assignment and input position unchanged and with the template’s
concatenated output appended to the existing output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Linear expression in the registers]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE}
\leanok
For $R \in \mathbb{N}$, a linear expression over $R$ registers is a pair
$(L, c)$ consisting of a finite list $L$ of register indices in
$\{0, \dots, R-1\}$, repetitions allowed, and a constant $c \in \mathbb{N}$; it
stands for the sum of the listed registers plus $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Value of a linear expression]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE.val}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE.val}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE}
Given register values $\rho : \{0,\dots,R-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a linear
expression $(L, c)$ with $L = (r_1, \dots, r_k)$, its value is the natural number
$\rho(r_1) + \dots + \rho(r_k) + c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Micro-operations printing a linear expression]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.linOps}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.linOps}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp}
For a linear expression $(L, c)$ over $R$ registers with $L = (r_1, \dots, r_k)$,
this is the list of template micro-operations $\mathsf{pr}(r_1), \dots,
\mathsf{pr}(r_k)$ (print each listed register in unary) followed by $c$ copies of
$\mathsf{out}(1)$ (print the bit $1$).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unary output from a linear expression]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.flatMap_exec_linOps}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.flatMap_exec_linOps}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.LinE, Complexity.CounterProg.LinE.val, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp.exec, Complexity.CounterProg.linOps}
\difficulty{4}
For any register values $\rho$ and linear expression $e$, concatenating the outputs of
the micro-operations associated with $e$ gives the unary bit string consisting of $e$
ones, where $e$ is evaluated at $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Micro-operations printing a fixed bit string]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.bitsOps}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.bitsOps}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp}
For a bit string $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$, this is the list of template
micro-operations $\mathsf{out}(w_1), \dots, \mathsf{out}(w_n)$, each printing one
bit of $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bit-string output from bit operations]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.flatMap_exec_bitsOps}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.flatMap_exec_bitsOps}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.MOp, Complexity.CounterProg.MOp.exec, Complexity.CounterProg.bitsOps}
\difficulty{3}
For any register values $\rho$ and bit string $w$, concatenating the outputs of the list
of bit-printing operations associated with the bits of $w$ gives exactly $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded-run Turing machine simulation]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.enc, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_of_halted, Complexity.CounterProg.run_succ, Complexity.CounterProg.sim_step, Complexity.CounterProg.step, Complexity.CounterProg.step_pos_le, Complexity.CounterProg.step_regs_le, Complexity.CounterProg.toTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $R,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite set of labels, let $P$ be a counter
program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, choose a start label
$\ell_0\in\Lambda$, and let $x$ be an input bit string. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and
abstract state $s$ whose read position is at most $|x|$ and whose registers satisfy
$s(r)+t\le B$ for every register $r$, there is a number of machine steps $t'\le t(2B+3)$
such that the compiled machine started at $\ell_0$, run on input $x$ from the encoding
of $s$, reaches the encoding of the state obtained by running $P$ on $x$ from $s$ for
$t$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Turing machine simulation of a halted run]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.exists_tm}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.exists_tm}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.enc, Complexity.CounterProg.init, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run, Complexity.CounterProg.toTM, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.UnaryTape.ones_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a finite label set, let $P$ be a
counter program over those registers and labels, let $\ell_0\in\Lambda$ be its start
label, and let $x$ be a bit string. If the counter program started in its initial state
is halted after $t$ steps, then the machine compiled from $P$ with start label $\ell_0$
computes the output of that run on input $x$ in exactly $t(2t+3)$ steps, with some space
usage.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on Input-Position Growth]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.run_pos_le}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.run_pos_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_succ, Complexity.CounterProg.run_zero, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program
over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, and fix an input bit string $x$. For every
abstract state $s$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the read position after $t$ steps from
$s$ is at most its initial read position plus $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output extension after one step]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.step_out}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.step_out}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter
program over them, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $s$ be an abstract state. There
exists a finite bit string $e$ such that the output after one step of $P$ on $x$ from
$s$ is the output of $s$ followed by $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output Is Extended by a Suffix]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.run_out}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.run_out}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_succ, Complexity.CounterProg.run_zero, Complexity.CounterProg.step, Complexity.CounterProg.step_out}
\difficulty{4}
Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program
over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, and fix an input bit string $x$. For every
abstract state $s$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a bit string $e$ such that the
output after $t$ steps from $s$ is its initial output followed by $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on one-step output growth]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.step_out_le}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.step_out_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter
program over them, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $s$ be an abstract state. For any
$K\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every register value in $s$ is at most $K$, the output after
one step of $P$ on $x$ from $s$ has length at most the length of the output of $s$ plus
$K+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output-Length Bound from the Initial State]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.run_init_out_le}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.run_init_out_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.init, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_add, Complexity.CounterProg.run_regs_le, Complexity.CounterProg.run_zero, Complexity.CounterProg.step, Complexity.CounterProg.step_out_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program
over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, and fix an input bit string $x$. For every
starting label $\ell_0\in\Lambda$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the output produced after
$t$ steps from the initial state at $\ell_0$ has length at most $t(t+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation under register bounds]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run_of_regs_le}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run_of_regs_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.enc, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_add, Complexity.CounterProg.run_succ, Complexity.CounterProg.run_zero, Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run, Complexity.CounterProg.step_pos_le, Complexity.CounterProg.toTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite set of labels, let $P$ be a counter
program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, choose a start label
$\ell_0\in\Lambda$, and let $x$ be an input bit string. For every $B,t\in\mathbb{N}$ and
abstract state $s$ with read position at most $|x|$, suppose that for every $j<t$ and
every register $r$, the value of register $r$ after $j$ steps of $P$ on $x$ from $s$ is
at most $B$. Then there exists $t'\le t(2B+5)$ such that the compiled machine started at
$\ell_0$, run on input $x$ from the encoding of $s$, reaches the encoding of the state
obtained after $t$ steps of $P$ on $x$ from $s$.
\end{theorem}
